title: Client decision lattice explorations
body:
Purpose:

Quick personal exploration of a client-side decision lattice that encodes trade-offs between latency, cost, and contextual completeness for prefetch + local warm strategies. This is a sketch for an API shape + runtime-config that downstream client libraries (mobile/web/edge) could implement. Not polished — mostly thinking out loud and a few examples to iterate with Diego/Rina.

Why a lattice?
- We want a compact representation that can express partial orders of preferences rather than a single linear priority list.
- Different apps (conversational agent, search autocomplete, summarizer) will have non-linear trade-offs: e.g., always-low-latency AND high-context completeness might be incompatible. Lattice lets us express multiple maximal configurations.

High level axes (first pass):
- latency_sensitivity: {low, medium, high}  -- maps to target p50/p95 bounds
- cost_taint: {free, balanced, conservative} -- preference for fewer upstream token calls
- context_fidelity: {minimal, anchored, full} -- how many external context fragments to include
- freshness: {stale_ok, prefer_fresh} -- whether to prefer cached responses
- local_memory_budget: integer (kb) -- client-local KV/embedding budget

Representation idea (JSON-ish lattice node):
{
  "node_id": "lat-high-cost-conservative-v1",
  "constraints": ["latency_sensitivity=high","context_fidelity=anchored"],
  "preferred_strategies": ["prefix_warmup","kv_local_lookup","prefer_quantized_variant"],
  "fallback_order": ["prefetch_small","on_demand_batch","server_streaming_fallback"]
}

API sketch (runtime decides what node to apply):
POST /client-config/v1/evaluate-node
Request body:
{
  "app_profile": "chat:assistant",
  "observed_metrics": { "p95_req_ms": 420, "tokens_per_min": 1200 },
  "hints": ["user_interaction_active","low_network_quality"],
  "client_state": { "local_memory_budget_kb": 512 }
}
Response (one candidate node, optionally several ranked):
{
  "candidates": [
    { "node_id": "lat-high-fresh-v3", "applied": true, "reason": "active interaction + poor net => prefer local prewarm" }
  ]
}

Runtime config snippet (client-local config file example):
# client-decision-lattice.yaml (informal)
latice_version: "0.2"
nodes:
  - id: "interactive-low-latency"
    constraints: ["latency_sensitivity=high","freshness=prefer_fresh"]
    strategies:
      - name: "kv_local_lookup"
        params: {ttl_s: 120, max_items: 100}
      - name: "partial_prefetch"
        params: {prefetch_tokens: 64, batch_size: 8}
    telemetry: {sample_rate: 0.02}
  - id: "background-sync-cheap"
    constraints: ["latency_sensitivity=low","cost_taint=free"]
    strategies:
      - name: "bulk_embedding_sync"
        params: {frequency_min: 60}
    telemetry: {sample_rate: 0.005}

Decision examples / scenarios:
1) New message arrives in chat, net flaky, user typing: choose node with latency_sensitivity=high + prefer_fresh => start prefix_warmup + kv_local_lookup; escalate to server_streaming_fallback if local warm fails.
2) Background summary job on low-cost tier: prefer background-sync-cheap node, perform bulk embedding sync only during wifi.

Fallback and graceful degradation:
- Each strategy must declare a compatibility set (which model variants it can use) and a budget token ceiling. If a strategy is unavailable, runtime walks the lattice to a less optimal superset node (partial order) and picks its top strategy.
- Maintain per-tenant counters to avoid cascading prefetch storms: prefetched_token_quota per-minute.

Instrumentation we need to make this actionable:
- Node apply events (reason + matched constraints)
- Strategy outcome events (started/failed/latency_ms/token_use)
- Local cache hit/miss + staleness metrics
- Backpressure signals (network quality, upstream throttle) correlated to node changes

Open questions / TODOs:
- How expressive should constraints be? Syntactic decisions: simple equality atoms vs small DSL (e.g., "latency_sensitivity >= medium"). Lean toward equality for client simplicity, leave richer predicates to server-side evaluation.
- Conflict resolution when multiple nodes match equally: tie-breaker by explicit ranking, then by recent success rate. Need to design decay window for success rates.
- Security/consent: if strategy requires sending extra context to server for prefetch, we must check consent flags (user opt-out). Add consent constraints to nodes.
- Edge cases: offline-first with local-only models. The lattice must include model capability attributes (local_model=true) so we can pick nodes that only use local inference.

Experiment ideas:
- A/B: show 3 lattice policies: (1) conservative-cost, (2) balanced, (3) latency-first. Measure user engagement delta, per-token cost, and p95 latency.
- Synthetic replay: feed historical session traces through lattice evaluator to estimate prefetched token volume and cache hit rates.

Notes to iteration with Diego/Rina:
- Need a compact prototype evaluator (JS/TS) that can run client-side to test several tie-break heuristics.
- Diego: can you wire up the session-trace CSV to simulate node transitions?
- Rina: can you draft a minimal telemetry schema (event names + fields) so we can instrument an Android client build for the experiment?

References / quick links: see linked_artifacts list. Also parity with server-side routing policy DSL (look at INF-2201) — want symmetrical semantics but reduced expressiveness on client.

Random scribbles (brain dump):
- Could reuse existing "prefetch_credit" concept from tenant-burst-reservation but with per-device lease semantics.
- Think about a small S-expression-ish compact encoding to push lattice diffs over the wire efficiently (e.g., "(node id constraints strategies)" ), but maybe premature optimization.

Next steps (short):
- Build TS prototype -> unit tests that replay 10k traces -> summarize prefetched token estimate. (owner: Aisha, target: 2 weeks)
- Telemetry schema draft (owner: Rina, target: 1 week)
- Design review with Diego + Runtime team (schedule week of Nov 25)

---
End of sketch. This file is my working brain dump; keep rough. Will refine into a formal spec if experiments show promise.
